result.builder:
Make one pull request that adds a --shout flag to greet-cli and meets every expect line of issue #12:
- node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
- without --shout the output is unchanged
- docs/index.md documents --shout
- after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Steps:
1. Read bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md, README.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml.
2. In bin/greet.js, detect `--shout` among the arguments (in any position relative to the name). When present, write the upper-cased greeting, so `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline. The name must still be the first argument that does not start with `--`, so `--shout` is never taken as the name. If you put the logic in src/greet.js, keep `greeting(name)` returning exactly `Hello, <name>!` when shouting is not asked for.
3. Without --shout, keep output byte-for-byte the same: `node bin/greet.js Ada` still prints `Hello, Ada!\n`, and the usage message and exit code 2 for a missing name stay the same.
4. Add tests in test/greet.test.js for the CLI with --shout (e.g. `['bin/greet.js', '--shout', 'Ada']` gives `HELLO, ADA!\n`, and `['bin/greet.js', 'Ada', '--shout']` gives the same). Keep the existing tests unchanged and passing.
5. Update docs/index.md to document the `--shout` flag: show the usage `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and say it prints the greeting in upper case (for example `HELLO, <NAME>!`). The literal text `--shout` must appear in the file.
6. The last expect line is met when the PR is merged: .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes the `docs/` directory to https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ on every push to main. Do not change that workflow and do not move the docs out of `docs/`. Keep the --shout documentation in docs/index.md so that it is published. In the PR description, say that the published-page line can only be confirmed after merge, once the pages workflow has run.
7. Run `npm test` and make sure it passes, then open the pull request.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head, run `npm install` if needed (the project has no dependencies), then run one check for each expect line, in order. Report PASS or FAIL for each, with the commands you ran and their output.

Check 1 — expect: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
Run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js --shout 'grace hopper'`.
PASS: stdout is the normal greeting in upper case, i.e. exactly `HELLO, ADA!` and `HELLO, GRACE HOPPER!` (each followed by a newline), and the exit code is 0.
FAIL: either output is not the upper-cased greeting (for example any lower-case letters, `--SHOUT` treated as the name, a usage error), or the exit code is not 0.

Check 2 — expect: "without --shout the output is unchanged"
Run `node bin/greet.js Ada` and `node bin/greet.js` (no name), and run `npm test`. For a baseline, run the same two commands at the PR's base commit (e.g. `git stash`-free: `git worktree add /tmp/greet-base <base-sha>` or `git show <base-sha>:bin/greet.js` with matching src) and compare.
PASS: `node bin/greet.js Ada` prints exactly `Hello, Ada!\n` with exit code 0, the no-name run prints the same stderr and exit code (2) as at the base, and the output matches the base byte for byte.
FAIL: any difference from the base in stdout, stderr or exit code for these runs.

Check 3 — expect: "docs/index.md documents --shout"
Run `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` and read the file.
PASS: docs/index.md contains `--shout` and describes what it does (prints the greeting in upper case).
FAIL: `--shout` is absent from docs/index.md, or the file mentions it without saying what it does.

Check 4 — expect: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"
This line can only be confirmed after the PR is merged and the pages workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml, which publishes `docs/` on push to main) has run. Find out whether the PR is merged (`gh pr view <number> --json state,mergedAt`) and, if merged, whether the pages workflow run for the merge commit has finished (`gh run list --workflow pages.yml`). Then fetch the page: `curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/` and search it for `--shout`.
PASS: the PR is merged and the fetched published page contains `--shout`.
FAIL: the fetched page does not contain `--shout`, or the page cannot be fetched. If the PR is not yet merged (or the pages run has not finished), report FAIL and state clearly that the reason is that this is a post-merge condition not yet met, not a defect in the diff.

Advisory
- Also try `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` (flag after the name); it should give `HELLO, ADA!`. Note the result but do not let it change Check 1.
- Confirm `npm test` passes and that new tests cover --shout.
- Confirm .github/workflows/pages.yml is unchanged and still publishes `docs/`, so a merge should make Check 4 pass.
